captions.instagram:
How does a motorcycle silencer work?

Each firing blasts a pulse of hot gas down the pipe, 50 times a second at 6,000 rpm. Cut open a motorcycle silencer in 3D and see how chambers, a resonator and fibre packing turn a 100 dB bang into a 77 dB hum, while a hot honeycomb cleans the gas.

→ A motorcycle exhaust is a valve, a pipe, a catalytic converter and a silencer.
→ Cut the silencer open: perforated tubes, walls, chambers and a wrap of wool.
→ Each firing sends a pressure pulse down the pipe: 50 a second at 6,000 rpm.
→ Chambers reflect it, a resonator cancels one note and packing soaks up the rest.
→ One cylinder thumps; four cylinders share the work and hum four times faster.

youtubeLong.title: How does a motorcycle silencer work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Each firing blasts a pulse of hot gas down the pipe, 50 times a second at 6,000 rpm. Cut open a motorcycle silencer in 3D and see how chambers, a resonator and fibre packing turn a 100 dB bang into a 77 dB hum, while a hot honeycomb cleans the gas.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/silencerclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/silencerclear

In this video:
• A valve, a pipe, a cleaner and a can. Burnt gas leaves the cylinder through the exhaust valve, runs down the header pipe, passes the catalytic converter and ends in the silencer.
• Three ways to tame a pulse. A four-stroke single fires rpm ÷ 120 times a second, sending sharp pressure pulses with a ladder of harmonics.
• Quiet costs back pressure. The walls and holes that stop sound also resist the gas, so quieter silencers usually mean more back pressure.
• A hot, precise chemical reactor. The catalytic converter is a honeycomb coated with platinum, palladium and rhodium.
• Loud silencers are illegal and harmful. New Indian two-wheelers must pass a 7.5 m pass-by test: 75, 77 or 80 dB(A) by engine size.
• From 1897 to BS-VI. The Reeves brothers patented a muffler of perforated shells in 1897, Maxim's 1909 silencer gave the part its British name, catalytic converters spread from 1975, and India set vehicle noise limits from 1990 and jumped to BS-VI in 2020.
